summary: The api component is the reason/LLM-IO stage of the loop: ApiClient (client.rs) sends the Message history to the model via chat (blocking) or chat_stream (SSE), returning a ChatResponse with Choices and Usage. tool_calling.rs extracts ToolCalls from native tool_calls or by robustly parsing model text, attach_tools puts ToolDefinitions on the request, and types.rs Message constructors plus validate_structure keep the wire format valid. RetryConfig backoff and a latched WallClockBudgetExceeded deadline guard every billable call, and StreamingResponse::collect reassembles StreamChunks into a canonical response.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with src/api/ read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), grounded in client.rs ApiClient/chat/chat_stream/RetryConfig/WallClockBudgetExceeded, types.rs Message/ChatResponse/Usage/ToolCall, streaming.rs StreamingResponse/StreamChunk, and tool_calling.rs extract_tool_calls/attach_tools.

examples.title: Fire one blocking reason turn with chat
examples.intent: Produce one model turn from the current conversation state.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ApiClient::chat posts the Message history and returns a ChatResponse whose first Choice carries the assistant Message; this is the reason step that yields either final text or ToolCalls for the act stage.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the Reason node fires a single ApiClient::chat request and lands the ChatResponse card beneath it.
touch_interaction.visual: The node spins while in flight and settles green when the ChatResponse arrives, red on an error kind.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop sends the history to ApiClient::chat, gets an assistant Message with two ToolCalls in its Choice, and hands them to dispatch.
examples.pitfall: Sending a history with no user Message can trigger a provider 400; validate_structure must pass before the request leaves.

examples.title: Stream a turn with chat_stream
examples.intent: Render partial output and tool calls as they arrive rather than blocking to completion.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ApiClient::chat_stream returns a StreamingResponse whose into_channel stream emits StreamChunk content, reasoning, tool-call and usage variants, letting the loop show progress and prepare the act stage before the turn finishes.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the Reason node opens a live token lane fed by StreamingResponse::into_channel that fills left to right as chunks arrive.
touch_interaction.visual: Content chunks type out in real time; a ToolCallDelta chunk pops a half-formed tool chip onto the lane.

examples.mini_scenario: The model streams reasoning then a tool call; the UI shows the text live while StreamChunk deltas queue the tool as it lands.
examples.pitfall: Failing to accumulate ToolCallDelta fragments by index yields a truncated, unparseable ToolCall.

examples.title: Collect a streamed turn into a full response
examples.intent: Reassemble streamed chunks into a single canonical assistant Message.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: StreamingResponse::collect drains the StreamChunk stream and merges content plus ToolCallDelta fragments into one ChatResponse, so downstream code treats streamed and blocking turns identically.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the stream lane collapses the chunk trail into a single settled ChatResponse card via collect.
touch_interaction.visual: Chunks converge and merge into one card with a completion checkmark and the finish_reason badge.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop streams for the UI but calls StreamingResponse::collect before dispatch, so the recovered ToolCalls are complete.
examples.pitfall: Reading content chunks but ignoring the accumulator loses tool-call fragments spread across ToolCallDelta values.

examples.title: Attach ToolDefinitions to the request
examples.intent: Tell the model which tools it may call this turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: attach_tools sets the request tools from the ToolDefinition/FunctionDefinition list and, when native function calling is on, enables automatic tool choice, shaping the model's available act surface for the reason turn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws edges from tool nodes into the Reason node to declare which ToolDefinitions attach_tools exposes this turn.
touch_interaction.visual: Each attached tool shows a small plug icon on the Reason node's rim with its FunctionDefinition name.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop attaches the critical tool's FunctionDefinition so the model can emit a native ToolCall for it.
examples.pitfall: Attaching the full tool catalog every turn wastes context; attach only what the turn needs.

examples.title: Extract tool calls, native first
examples.intent: Get structured ToolCalls out of the model turn regardless of format.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: extract_tool_calls reads message.tool_calls when present and otherwise falls back to extract_tool_calls_from_text, so both native-FC and text-only models feed the same act stage.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the response card splits out the ToolCall chips extract_tool_calls recovered.
touch_interaction.visual: Native calls render with a solid plug icon; text-parsed calls render with a dashed 'recovered' icon.

examples.mini_scenario: A model without native FC emits a JSON block in text; extract_tool_calls_from_text recovers the ToolCall and the loop runs it.
examples.pitfall: Assuming native tool_calls exist for every model drops the calls of text-only backends entirely.

examples.title: Robustly parse tool calls from text
examples.intent: Recover tool calls even when the model wraps them in prose or slightly malformed JSON.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: extract_tool_calls_from_text delegates to the tool parser and parsed_to_tool_call assigns a synthetic id, so imperfect model output still becomes a valid ToolCall for the act stage.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a recovered tool chip shows the raw text span parsed_to_tool_call built it from.
touch_interaction.visual: Recovered chips carry a repair-wrench badge and a tooltip with the source span.

examples.mini_scenario: The model emits a fenced JSON tool call inside a paragraph; extract_tool_calls_from_text recovers it and parsed_to_tool_call mints the id.
examples.pitfall: A non-unique synthetic id collides tool results and breaks call-to-result pairing on the next turn.

examples.title: Feed a tool result back as a tool message
examples.intent: Close the act-to-reason loop by returning execution output to the model.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Message::tool binds role='tool' content to its tool_call_id so the next chat turn perceives the outcome and reasons about the next move.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws an edge from a tool result card back into the Message history strip feeding the next turn.
touch_interaction.visual: The Message::tool bubble renders grey, tagged with the tool_call_id it answers.

examples.mini_scenario: cargo_test output is wrapped via Message::tool keyed to its call id and the model reads it on the next ApiClient::chat turn.
examples.pitfall: A tool Message whose tool_call_id matches no prior ToolCall is rejected by strict providers.

examples.title: Validate message structure before sending
examples.intent: Keep the request in a shape providers accept.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Message::validate_structure and validate check the history built from Message::system/user/assistant constructors, catching orphan tool messages and bad ordering so the reason turn never dies on a provider 400.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User flicks the history strip to run validate_structure; invalid bubbles fly to a problem tray.
touch_interaction.visual: Valid bubbles glow a steady border; structural violations flash red with the failing rule label.

examples.mini_scenario: A resumed history with a dangling tool Message fails validate_structure and is repaired before the request is sent.
examples.pitfall: Skipping validation on resumed histories can send an out-of-order payload that the provider rejects.

examples.title: Carry reasoning on tool-only assistant turns
examples.intent: Avoid provider 400s when the assistant turn has no visible text.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Message::assistant_with_reasoning stores the reasoning trace alongside empty content, so a tool-only assistant turn still forms a valid Message for the next request instead of an empty bubble.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping an empty assistant bubble fills it with the reasoning carried by assistant_with_reasoning.
touch_interaction.visual: Empty bubbles show a hollow outline that fills solid once the reasoning is attached.

examples.mini_scenario: A tool-only turn has empty content; Message::assistant_with_reasoning keeps the trace so the next request stays valid.
examples.pitfall: Leaving assistant content empty makes some providers 400 and stalls the loop mid-turn.

examples.title: Account tokens with Usage
examples.intent: Track how much budget each reason turn consumes.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The ChatResponse carries Usage (prompt/completion/total tokens); the loop adds it to the cumulative budget that guards iteration and wall-clock stops.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the Reason node reveals a Usage meter for the last turn and the running total.
touch_interaction.visual: A dual bar shows prompt vs completion tokens; it deepens red as the cumulative total climbs.

examples.mini_scenario: Each turn's Usage is summed so the loop knows when it is nearing its token budget and can stop early.
examples.pitfall: Trusting a Usage where total != prompt + completion corrupts budget accounting downstream.

examples.title: Capture the full turn trace with chat_with_meta
examples.intent: Record exactly what was sent and how the turn resolved.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ApiClient::chat_with_meta and chat_stream_with_meta return a ChatMetadata (request body, elapsed time, finish reason, token counts) alongside the response, giving the learn stage a full trace of each reason turn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the Reason node opens the ChatMetadata drawer with the request body and timing.
touch_interaction.visual: A ledger badge shows elapsed ms and finish_reason; slow turns glow amber.

examples.mini_scenario: A turn is logged via chat_with_meta with its finish_reason and elapsed time so a stall can later be diagnosed.
examples.pitfall: Logging the raw request body without redaction can leak the credential into the trace.

examples.title: Retry transient failures with RetryConfig
examples.intent: Survive transient 429/5xx without failing the whole turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: with_retry_config installs a RetryConfig that retries retryable statuses with backoff, so a flaky provider does not immediately push the loop into ErrorRecovery.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the Reason node opens the RetryConfig dial for max attempts and delay.
touch_interaction.visual: During retries the node shows a countdown ring for the backoff window.

examples.mini_scenario: A 429 makes the client wait out the RetryConfig backoff then retry, and the turn succeeds on attempt two.
examples.pitfall: Retrying non-retryable statuses wastes budget; keep the RetryConfig status list conservative.

examples.title: Latch the wall-clock deadline across calls
examples.intent: Bound total LLM-IO time even across retries and multiple turns.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The wall-clock deadline is latched on the first billable request and shared across all retries and calls; once expired, WallClockBudgetExceeded is raised before any new request as a budget stop, not a network error.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating a dial on the Reason node sets the shared wall-clock ceiling guarding every ApiClient call.
touch_interaction.visual: A clock ring shared across turns drains and locks red when WallClockBudgetExceeded trips.

examples.mini_scenario: Mid-run the wall budget expires; the next chat call is refused with WallClockBudgetExceeded, classified as a budget stop.
examples.pitfall: Classifying a wall-budget stop as a network error mislabels the failure mode and triggers pointless retries.

examples.title: Shrink an oversized history with strip_images
examples.intent: React to a too-large request by slimming the payload rather than dying.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: When the request would exceed the window, Message::strip_images drops heavy ImageUrl blocks from history and validate re-checks the result, letting the loop retry the reason turn smaller instead of failing.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: On overflow the history strip auto-pinches, shedding ImageUrl thumbnails before the request is retried.
touch_interaction.visual: The node flashes an overflow badge, image blocks fold away, and the turn re-fires.

examples.mini_scenario: A multimodal history overflows the window; strip_images removes old screenshots, validate passes, and chat succeeds.
examples.pitfall: Retrying the same oversized payload unchanged guarantees the same failure; always shrink before resend.

examples.title: Dial reasoning depth with ThinkingMode
examples.intent: Control how much hidden reasoning the model spends per turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ThinkingMode (enabled, disabled, or a token budget) shapes the reasoning depth of each turn, trading token spend for deliberation on hard steps.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the Reason node dials ThinkingMode from off to a token budget for deeper reasoning.
touch_interaction.visual: Higher thinking deepens the node color and opens a separate reasoning stream lane.

examples.mini_scenario: For a tricky refactor the loop sets a ThinkingMode budget so the model reasons harder before acting.
examples.pitfall: Leaving a large thinking budget on for trivial turns wastes tokens the loop budget cannot spare.

examples.title: Attach an image with user_multimodal
examples.intent: Let the model see a screenshot or diagram as part of the reason turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Message::user_multimodal builds a Message with ContentBlock text plus ImageUrl parts; has_images and image_count let the loop track how much visual payload the history carries.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User drags an image thumbnail onto the Reason node, wrapping it into a user_multimodal Message.
touch_interaction.visual: The bubble gains an image thumbnail chip; image_count badges the history strip.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator drops a UI screenshot on the node; Message::user_multimodal attaches it and the model critiques the layout.
examples.pitfall: Images bloat token counts fast — check image_count before the request or the turn overflows the window.

examples.title: Detect the backend before the first call
examples.intent: Pick the right request shape for the actual provider behind the endpoint.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ApiClient::detect_backend identifies which backend the endpoint speaks, so from_settings can build a client whose chat/completion paths match the provider's capabilities before any billable call.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the Reason node's endpoint chip runs detect_backend and shows the identified provider.
touch_interaction.visual: The chip fills with the provider's badge; an unknown backend shows a question-mark outline.

examples.mini_scenario: At startup detect_backend identifies the endpoint, and from_settings builds an ApiClient tuned to it.
examples.pitfall: Assuming every endpoint is fully OpenAI-compatible sends fields the backend rejects on turn one.

examples.title: Use the completion path for raw text backends
examples.intent: Keep reasoning working on backends that only expose text completion.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ApiClient::completion sends a CompletionRequest and returns a CompletionResponse with CompletionChoices, giving the loop a reason path when chat-style tool calling is unavailable.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the Reason node sideways swaps it from chat mode to the completion lane.
touch_interaction.visual: The node re-tints to show the completion path; tool chips gain a 'text-parse' watermark.

examples.mini_scenario: detect_backend finds a completion-only server; the loop routes through ApiClient::completion and parses tool calls from text.
examples.pitfall: Do not attach_tools on a completion-only backend — the field is ignored and tool calls must come from text parsing.

examples.title: Build the client from settings with a profile
examples.intent: Construct one correctly configured client from the resolved config.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ApiClient::from_settings builds the client from config, chat_with_profile selects a named profile for a turn, and config() exposes the resolved settings — a foundation seam every reason turn depends on.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the Reason node lists profiles; tapping one re-arms the node for chat_with_profile.
touch_interaction.visual: The node's base ring shows the active profile name; switching profiles cross-fades the ring color.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop builds the client via from_settings, then runs one hard turn through chat_with_profile with the deep-reasoning profile.
examples.pitfall: Constructing ad-hoc clients with ApiClient::new in multiple places drifts retry/endpoint settings apart.

examples.title: Emit request progress to the perceive frame
examples.intent: Show request lifecycle events without changing the reason result.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: with_progress_emitter attaches an emitter to the ApiClient so each chat/chat_stream call reports progress events the UI renders; it observes the reason stage without altering its output.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch-in on the Reason node expands the progress emitter's event feed for the in-flight request.
touch_interaction.visual: A side rail ticks off send/wait/first-byte events; the node halo breathes while waiting.

examples.mini_scenario: With with_progress_emitter attached, the UI shows 'request sent, awaiting first byte' during a slow chat_stream turn.
examples.pitfall: The emitter must never block the request path — a slow observer stalls every billable turn.
